problem: Detecting AI-generated videos is difficult because pixel-domain methods overlook generative artifacts encoded in compressed bitstreams.
approach: STREAM operates directly on compressed bitstreams, using I-frames, motion vectors, and residual errors to detect spatiotemporal artifacts through a motion-guided alignment module and gated fusion mechanism.
contribution: Achieves SOTA detection with mAP of 0.965 and 2.5× faster inference than previous baselines.

problem: Evaluating causal claims is hard without ground truth, especially when assessing collections of bivariate statements.
approach: Develops a compatibility score that quantifies plausibility of induced multivariate causal models by measuring implausible additional confounding, without requiring faithfulness.
contribution: Provides theoretical and empirical evidence that compatibility and incompatibility scores distinguish correct from incorrect causal statements, with application to evaluating LLM-generated causal claims.

problem: Low-rank Hankel matrix completion requires balancing first-order algorithmic efficiency with fast convergence independent of condition number.
approach: Uses Jacobi-preconditioned gradient descent with a generator mapping factor-based iterates to matrix space, establishing equivalence with manifold-based methods.
contribution: Achieves linear convergence independent of condition number while maintaining low per-iteration complexity across broad problem settings.

problem: Current LLM agent privacy defenses are static and reactive, failing to support proactive context-aware privacy decisions during multi-step execution.
approach: Proposes Contextualized Defense Instructing (CDI) where an instructor model generates step-specific privacy guidance via reinforcement learning, trained on failure trajectories.
contribution: CDI achieves 94.2% privacy preservation and 80.6% helpfulness with superior robustness to adversarial conditions compared to baseline defenses.

problem: Federated learning under non-IID data suffers from bias toward skewed majority clients when using fixed neighborhood structures for skew estimation.
approach: FedVeer uses self-adaptive kernel density estimation with k-free neighborhoods determined via max-margin learning, plus Kalman filtering for stability.
contribution: Achieves up to 6.36% accuracy improvement and reduces noise-induced degradation by up to 6.01% on real-world datasets.

problem: Graph transport methods fail to generalize across sparse topologies and scale poorly with graph size and time horizon.
approach: GSBoG learns executable controlled continuous-time Markov chain policies on arbitrary graphs via likelihood optimization of trajectory-level behaviors under state cost augmented dynamics.
contribution: Reliably learns accurate, topology-respecting policies optimizing application-specific intermediate state costs on real-world graph topologies.

problem: Continual learning methods that mitigate forgetting often suffer from singular value collapse in gradients, reducing model plasticity.
approach: PAPO augments gradients with polar operators to activate suppressed directions: G ← G + λ·polar(G), approximated via Polar Express using only matrix operations.
contribution: On MiniImageNet, PAPO integrated into ER, MAS, GPM, and TRGP produces accuracy gains of 9.01%, 4.76%, 8.90%, and 9.19% respectively.

problem: Chain-of-thought monitoring for AI agents may be fragile under different training procedures and scaling, yet its reliability is underexplored.
approach: Proposes three evaluation archetypes (intervention, process, outcome-property), studies monitorability across model sizes and reasoning compute, and tests if follow-up questions improve monitoring.
contribution: Shows frontier models are generally monitorable, longer CoTs improve monitorability, and smaller models at higher reasoning effort can achieve better monitoring at greater cost.

problem: AI training carbon emissions lack systematic accounting methods, leaving questions about current and future environmental impact.
approach: Estimates aggregate training emissions of Hugging Face open-source models using metadata with tiered handling of incomplete disclosure, introduces AI Training Carbon Intensity (ATCI) metric.
contribution: Shows training popular open-source models resulted in approximately 6.0×10^4 metric tons of carbon emissions, providing scalable framework for emission estimation.

problem: Statement autoformalization treats formal code as flat sequences, neglecting the hierarchical logic inherent in mathematical statements.
approach: DSR decomposes statements into logical components, maps them to structured operator trees, and uses sub-tree refinement to localize and repair errors.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on PRIME benchmark of 156 theorems, consistently outperforming baselines under equivalent computational budgets.

problem: Disentangling memorization from generalization in language models is difficult, making model capacity estimates unreliable.
approach: Proposes method that separates memorization into unintended memorization and generalization by eliminating generalization, enabling total memorization measurement.
contribution: Estimates GPT-style models have capacity of approximately 3.6 bits per parameter; models memorize until capacity fills then transition to generalization.

problem: Model upscaling can be sensitive to hyperparameters at target size, and scaling law extrapolation from smaller models is theoretically unclear.
approach: Introduces principled width-based upscaling using theoretically grounded, width-dependent scalings for perturbation and optimizer hyperparameters based on μP theory.
contribution: Proves upscaled models are functionally equivalent under zero perturbation and establishes hyperparameter transfer enabling efficient tuning with reduced cost.

problem: Converting pretrained Softmax attention to linear-complexity attention causes severe accuracy degradation due to representational gap.
approach: SD3.5-T^5 uses Test-Time Training with structural alignment to Softmax attention and architectural modifications (key instance normalization, locality enhancement) for representational alignment.
contribution: Linearizes Stable Diffusion 3.5 with comparable quality at 1.32× and 1.47× speedup at 1K and 2K resolutions using only 1 hour fine-tuning on 4 H20 GPUs.

problem: Existing adaptive methods like Adam use coordinate-wise adaptation unsuitable for matrix optimization, while spectral methods lack connection to variance adaptation.
approach: DeVA reformulates AdaGrad into decoupled variance adaptation and scale-invariant terms, bridging vector-based and matrix spectral optimization.
contribution: Consistently outperforms Muon and SOAP, reducing token usage by around 6.6% on language modeling and image classification.

problem: Long-horizon interactive agent benchmarks underrepresent global constraints, multi-tool coordination, and adapting to evolving user behavior.
approach: TRIP-Bench offers travel-planning scenarios with real-world data, 18 tools, 40+ requirements, and spans up to 15 user turns with 150+ tool calls; proposes GTPO online RL method.
contribution: Even advanced models achieve at most 50% on easy split; GTPO improves constraint satisfaction and robustness in Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct.

problem: Semi-supervised inference in biomedical research struggles with unstructured data and covariate misalignment across datasets.
approach: Integrates LLMs to extract features from unstructured data with systematic pseudo-label calibration via novel prediction-invariance identification strategy.
contribution: Improves parameter estimation efficiency while maintaining full statistical validity despite mismatched covariates between labeled and unlabeled datasets.

problem: Functional equivalence in Transformers is complex due to positional encodings, and their effect on model expressivity and mode connectivity is unclear.
approach: Provides formal analysis of functional equivalence with sinusoidal and rotary positional encodings (RoPE), showing RoPE reduces symmetry group.
contribution: Shows sinusoidal encodings preserve vanilla attention equivalence while rotary encodings enhance expressivity, explaining RoPE's growing prominence.

problem: Semi-supervised 3D medical segmentation progress is clouded by confirmation bias in pseudo-labeling and overfitting via test-set validation.
approach: Proposes TCSeg with tri-space calibration decoupling confidence from uncertainty, collaboratively correcting bias across feature, probability, and image spaces.
contribution: Delivers strong performance under existing protocols; advocates for multiple-run reporting to establish more rigorous benchmarks with realistic perspective.

problem: Token-wise temperature scaling in discrete sequence models induces bias in MAP estimates and is not tractable for sequence-level adjustment.
approach: Proposes fine-tuning objectives for sequence-level temperature scaling unified across autoregressive and diffusion models, with metrics based on likelihood ratios.
contribution: Achieves consistent generation with lower perplexity on GPT2 and BD3LM; provides evidence of enhanced reasoning performance.

problem: Lean theorem-proving benchmarks are treated as reliable despite potential dataset defects and evaluation failures that inflate or deflate scores.
approach: Audits five widely used benchmarks with corpus-scale static checkers, surfaces 4,833 findings including 398 mechanically certified issues (counterexamples, vacuous theorems, unsound axioms).
contribution: Proposes fault taxonomy, automated checkers, semantic audit prompts, and standards for formal math dataset creation; releases corrected snapshots.

problem: Quantization hyperparameter effects (bit width, range) on learning dynamics and STE training remain largely unexplored.
approach: Shows STE dynamics converge to a deterministic ODE in high-dimensional limit, with plateau length depending on quantization range.
contribution: Reveals STE training exhibits plateau then sharp drop in error; fixed-point analysis quantifies asymptotic deviation from unquantized models.

problem: Directly sparsifying pretrained dense attention into dilated patterns causes severe accuracy loss, preventing flexible inference-time reuse.
approach: RAT+ trains densely with full-sequence recurrence and active recurrence learning, then switches at inference to dilated or hybrid compositions with minimal adaptation.
contribution: At 1.5B parameters, matches dense accuracy at D=16 and drops 2-3 points at D=64; achieves 64× reduction in attention FLOPs and KV cache at D=64.

problem: Post-Training Quantization for diffusion LLMs is prone to frontier decision flips that are irreversibly locked in, causing cascading errors.
approach: FAIR-Calib uses two-stage PTQ with position prior combining frontier hits and reliability, performing layer-wise calibration on reweighted hidden-state MSE.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines on LLaDA and Dream (W4A4), significantly reducing frontier flips and post-commit mismatches.

problem: Separate estimation of multiple dynamic treatment policies prevents information sharing, inducing structurally uncontrolled second-order bias.
approach: PEQ-Net uses policy-aware reparameterization of Q-functions with shared policy encoder trained via kernel mean embeddings, followed by LTMLE correction.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing ICE-based methods with substantial RMSE reductions, particularly when evaluating closely related policies.

problem: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards faces tradeoff between token-level fine-grained credit assignment and sequence-level stability.
approach: TGPO integrates sequence anchors aligning updates with stable reference and trust-based information gates modulating token-level signal contribution.
contribution: Consistently enhances learning efficiency across seven mathematical reasoning datasets, improving gradient utilization while maintaining stable optimization.

problem: Creating editable scientific illustrations remains labor-intensive and existing generative models produce raster outputs lacking vector editability.
approach: LiveFigure uses VLM agents imitating multi-step research workflows: planning from references, generating executable PowerPoint scripts, refining with visual diagnostics.
contribution: Achieves 80% publication-readiness in only 17 manual edits versus 24% for baselines; generates fully vectorized, editable publication-ready figures.

problem: High-quality training datasets for reasoning require costly human annotation, and synthesis methods face tradeoff between structural validity and complexity.
approach: Agentic Proposing models synthesis as goal-driven sequential decision where agents dynamically select and compose modular reasoning skills via internal reflection.
contribution: 30B solver trained on 11,000 synthesized trajectories achieves 91.6% on AIME25, rivaling frontier models and demonstrating synthetic data can substitute for massive human curation.

problem: Hypergraph neural networks suffer from rank collapse and hyperedge semantic dependency in two-stage message passing.
approach: MC-HNN introduces multi-channel message passing maintaining high-rank representations and latent hyperedge type encoding injecting independent degrees of freedom.
contribution: Alleviates rank collapse and semantic dependency bottlenecks, achieving strong empirical performance on hypergraph tasks.

problem: Exact posterior computation is intractable, and existing approximate inference methods are computationally expensive or require costly retraining on prior changes.
approach: Distribution Transformer learns distribution-to-distribution mappings using Gaussian Mixture Models with self and cross-attention, enabling prior-to-posterior transformation.
contribution: Reduces computation from minutes to milliseconds while achieving expected log-likelihood performance on par with or superior to existing methods.

problem: Understanding how auto-regressive models learn latent state representations from partially observed linear systems remains theoretically unclear.
approach: Shows two-layer linear auto-regressive models trained by ERM naturally approximate Kalman filtering, with benign optimization landscape and finite-sample guarantees.
contribution: Demonstrates learned hidden representations coincide with Kalman filter state estimates up to similarity transformation, with theoretical convergence guarantees.

problem: Language models in healthcare struggle with trustworthiness across low-resource languages despite global adoption needs.
approach: CLINIC benchmarks LMs across truthfulness, fairness, safety, robustness, and privacy through 18 diverse tasks spanning 15 languages and healthcare topics.
contribution: Reveals LMs struggle with factual correctness, demonstrate demographic and linguistic bias, and remain vulnerable to privacy breaches and adversarial attacks.

problem: Sequential recommendation models have limited flexibility responding to immediate user requests without costly retraining or inference overhead.
approach: CRAMER treats user requests as control signals modulating frozen backbone parameters through request-aware masking inspired by control theory.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art baselines with minimal overhead; exhibits enhanced controllability and cross-domain adaptability.

problem: Distillation claims about efficiency rarely account for full end-to-end energy costs including teacher-side workloads like data generation and evaluation.
approach: Presents comprehensive energy accounting framework tracking GPU power consumption across distillation phases, constructing energy-quality-throughput Pareto frontiers.
contribution: Reveals previously ignored teacher-side costs and derives practical design rules for selecting distillation methods under energy constraints.

problem: Structure-Based Drug Design mismatch between separate continuous and discrete probability paths ignores underlying statistical manifolds.
approach: EvoEGF-Mol represents molecules via composite exponential-family distributions evolving along exponential geodesics under Fisher-Rao metric with dynamic target distributions.
contribution: Approaches reference PoseBusters passing rate of 93.4% on CrossDock with geometric precision, achieving superior performance on real-world MolGenBench tasks.

problem: Layer pruning in LLMs triggers sudden performance collapse, and representation-based analyses fail to explain the mechanism.
approach: Proposes decision representation framework introducing Decision Margin and Option Frequency metrics, partitioning networks into Silent Phase and Decisive Phase.
contribution: Shows pruning Decisive Phase has minimal impact but Silent Phase pruning triggers immediate collapse, revealing extreme sensitivity of decision transition.

problem: Q-learning is slow as values move from initialization near zero to true values, and algorithms update action-values independently without sharing value structure.
approach: Mean-expansion layer shares values across actions within a state and learns lower-norm representation, accelerating learning as parameter-free addition to Q-networks.
contribution: Improves aggregate performance across 57 Atari games, increases action gaps, and dramatically reduces value overestimation.

problem: Low-precision deep learning suffers instability despite energy efficiency gains, requiring better algorithmic stabilization.
approach: Log-Normal Multiplicative Dynamics (LMD) incorporates biological synaptic properties via variational Bayesian formulation with log-normal posterior over weights.
contribution: Successfully trains Vision Transformers and GPT-2 from scratch with low-precision forward-pass multiplications.

problem: Existing SLAM approaches produce maps lacking geometric fidelity required for reliable downstream perception.
approach: UniMapping constructs persistent neural-descriptor map from multimodal observations using Spatial-Aware Deformable Transformer with explicit geometric inductive bias.
contribution: Achieves competitive SLAM performance; significantly enhances downstream tasks with mAP +3.1% and mIoU +7.1% via accumulated multi-view context.

problem: Zeroth-order optimization for LLM fine-tuning relies on hand-crafted static sampling strategies unadapted to model-specific structures.
approach: ZO-Finetuner learns efficient perturbation strategies through compact memory-efficient design, supporting one-time per-model training with reuse across tasks.
contribution: Outperforms prior zeroth-order baselines in 82.1% of task-model combinations across 4 LLMs and 7 datasets.

problem: Multi-objective RL with reactive preference adversaries needs time-consistent robustness models with tractable weight selection dynamics.
approach: Studies Bellman-Isaacs recursion where opponent chooses weights with switching cost based on Bregman divergence, solving via Bregman-prox updates.
contribution: Develops BR-K evaluation testing policies against independent best-response adversaries, improving WRR under step-wise opponents.
